index_record.dataset_generation_caption: The figure illustrates the sequential, iterative process of online Bayesian inference, structured as a horizontal flow diagram progressing from left to right. The global layout consists of two parallel rows: the top row represents incoming observations at discrete time steps, while the bottom row represents the evolving posterior means updated at each step. The process begins on the far left with an initial prior mean, denoted by a diamond-shaped node labeled μ₀. This node is connected via a solid arrow to the next diamond-shaped node labeled μ₁, indicating the first update. Above μ₁, a circular node labeled y₁ represents the first observation, with a downward arrow pointing to μ₁, signifying that this observation is used to update the posterior mean. This pattern continues: each subsequent diamond node (μ₂, μ₃, etc.) receives an update from the corresponding observation (y₂, y₃, etc.), which is represented by a circle above it and a downward arrow connecting them. The diamond nodes are uniformly shaped, outlined in black, and filled with white; they contain bold, italicized Greek letters (μ₀, μ₁, μ₂, μ₃, ...) centered within. The circular observation nodes are also uniformly shaped, outlined in black, and filled with light gray; they contain bold, italicized lowercase letters (y₁, y₂, y₃, ...) centered within. The connections between nodes are solid black arrows with filled triangular heads, indicating the direction of information flow. Horizontal arrows connect successive posterior mean nodes (μ₀ → μ₁ → μ₂ → μ₃ → ...), showing the temporal progression of the update sequence. Vertical arrows point from each observation node (y₁, y₂, y₃, ...) down to the corresponding posterior mean node (μ₁, μ₂, μ₃, ...), illustrating how each new observation contributes to updating the current belief state. The sequence terminates with an ellipsis (...) inside both a diamond and a circle, indicating that the process continues indefinitely. The caption clarifies that at each time step t, observation y_t is incorporated to update the posterior mean μ_t, and the ellipsis denotes the iterative nature of the updates, beginning from the prior mean μ₀.
